newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-BLAYLOCK FREE THROWS GIVE HAWKS SEVENTH CONSECUTIVE WIN.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-BLAYLOCK FREE THROWS GIVE HAWKS SEVENTH CONSECUTIVE WIN.

text.p: Mookie Blaylock sank two free throws with half a second left on the clock to lift the the Atlanta Hawks to their seventh straight victory, a 95-93 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves on a perfect night for the home teams in the NBA.
Steve Smith scored 26 points, Christian Laettner added 22 and Blaylock had 16 points for the Hawks, who have won 14 in a row in Atlanta since losing their home opener.

Blaylock drove to the basket and was fouled by Minnesota's Sam Mitchell with 0.5 seconds to go. After Blaylock made both shots, Mitchell got the ball to rookie guard Shane Heal, who could not get off a shot.
Tom Gugliotta scored 22 points and grabbed 12 boards and Kevin Garnett added 22 and 10 for Minnesota.
"It's just a game where we played hard all game," said Laettner, who fouled out with 50 seconds left. "It was back-and-forth and the guys came through."
The Timberwolves shot 52 percent (31-of-60) from the field, compared to Atlanta's 39 percent (33-of-85).
"They got 25 more shots than us," Garnett said. "We can't let this get us down."
In Chicago, Michael Jordan scored 10 of his 39 points in the final 3 1/2 minutes as the Bulls extended their winning streak to seven by edging the Washington Bullets 108-107.
Jordan scored 10 of the final 15 points for Chicago, which squandered a nine-point fourth-quarter lead but regrouped to improve to a league-best 18-1 at home.

Scottie Pippen added 25 points for the Bulls, including three three-pointers in the final period, and Dennis Rodman grabbed 18 rebounds, including the 10,000th of his career to become the 24th NBA player to reach the plateau.
Chris Webber had 33 points, 10 rebounds and seven assists for the Bullets.
In Phoenix, Kevin Johnson had 25 points and 16 assists and Cedric Ceballos scored seven of his 23 in the fourth quarter to lead the Suns to a 110-101 win over the Denver Nuggets.
Johnson's 11th assist of the game was the 6,000th of his career, making him the 16th player in NBA history to accomplish that feat.
Ceballos scored four points in an 8-2 spurt a the Suns opened a 103-93 advantage with 2:36 to go.
Laphonso Ellis tied a career-high with 33 points and Dale Ellis added 24 for the Nuggets, who have lost five straight and nine of 10.
In Sacramento, Mitch Richmond scored seven of his 37 points in overtime and keyed a game-ending 8-0 run as the Kings knocked off the Indiana Pacers, 105-98.
Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf had 17 points and Olden Polynice added 14 for the Kings, who were 7-for-10 from three-point range compared to just 1-of-7 from beyond the arc for the Pacers.
Antonio Davis scored 30 points and Reggie Miller added 21 for Indiana, which has lost five of its last six road games.
In Houston, Charles Barkley had 29 points and 12 rebounds as the Rockets beat the New York Knicks for the first time since Game Seven of the 1994 NBA Finals, 106-86.
Clyde Drexler had 19 points and nine assists and Hakeem Olajuwon added 15 points for the Rockets, who outscored the Knicks 33-19 in the second quarter to lead 63-43 at the half.
Houston outmuscled New York, grabbing 49 rebounds and holding the Knicks to a season-low 29 after losing their last four meetings with New York since winning the 1994 championship.
In Boston, Rick Fox scored 10 of his 23 points in the fourth quarter to help the Celtics record a a 116-108 victory over the Golden State Warriors.
David Wesley, who scored Boston's first nine points of the final quarter, and Eric Williams added 21 points apiece for the Celtics, who won for just the fourth time in 15 games.
Joe Smith scored 33 points and Latrell Sprewell added 32 for the Warriors, losers of five of their last seven games.
In Portland, Isaiah Rider scored 22 points and Arvydas Sabonis had 16 points and 13 rebounds to lead the Trail Blazers to a 95-86 over the Detroit Pistons.
Kenny Anderson added 14 points and dished out 12 assists for Portland, which won for the sixth time in seven games.
Terry Mills scored 24 points and Grant Hill had 20 points, 10 rebounds and nine assists for Detroit, which lost for just the second time in eight games.
In Los Angeles, Shaquille O'Neal scored 24 points and grabbed 12 rebounds as the Lakers beat the Vancouver Grizzlies for the sixth time in as many meetings, 91-81.
Roy Rogers made an 11-footer to give the Grizziles their last lead at 69-68 with 10:46 left. But Los Angeles outscored Vancouver 23-12 the rest of the way.
Anthony Peeler had 23 points and Shareef Abdur-Rahim added 19 for the Grizzlies, who have lost eight of their last nine games and fell to 2-15 on the road.
